To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lakes and lake fills have an important influence on the development of fluvial distributory channels.
organic–clastic lakes and their fills influence distributary channel architecture and processes.
the development of distributary channel belts in the distal part of the delta plain of the Rhine–Meuser delta is affected by organic–clastic lacustrine lake fills.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of organic–clastic lacustrine deposits on distributary processes.
the role of organic and clastic lake fill in the development of fluvial distributory channel architecture.
the interaction of lake fills and distributary channels and the influence of this interaction on the development of fluvial architecture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
organic–clastic lacustrine deposits in distal delta plains are a key factor in controlling channel patterns and sedimentology.
organic–clastic lacustrine fills have a major influence on distributary fluvial processes.
organic–clastic lacustrine fills influence fluvial processes by changing the substrate and thus the channel pattern and sedimentary characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lakes and lake fills are an integral part of the distal delta plain, which influences fluvial processes and sedimentology.
the influence of organic–clastic lacustrine deposits is more important than previously thought.
lakes and lake fills influence the development of fluvial distributory channel architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lakes and fossil lakes can influence the sedimentary architecture of fluvial distributory systems.
the presence of lake fills and organic–clastic deposits can influence the development of distributary channel belts and their sedimentary architecture.
the influence of organic–clastic fills on fluvio-lacustrine systems is not restricted to the proximal zone of deltas.
